notes: Prompts are run against the live supersimplesuper/code board, so exact PR numbers drift. Assertions target structural correctness (chain reconstruction, bottleneck identification, the no-merge-downward rule) rather than specific PR states.

evals.name: full-board-with-stacks
evals.prompt: can you please look at all my PRs on github, and give me a summary of where each of them is at? A few of them are stacked branches, and I don't want to merge them down onto branches that have not yet been reviewed (because that will make the review process longer, and mean re-reviewing code that's already been approved)
evals.expected_output: A grouped report: PRs ready to merge now, one section per stacked chain ordered bottom to top, standalone PRs needing review, and a suggested merge order. Each chain names its bottleneck and any approved PRs stranded above it.
assertions: Reconstructs the stacked chains from base/head branch names rather than listing PRs flat
Orders each chain bottom to top, root first
Names the bottleneck PR for each chain, meaning the lowest PR that is not ready
Identifies approved PRs stranded above a bottleneck
States that merging an upper PR down into its base would force re-review of already-approved code
Recommends a concrete merge order starting with PRs that are approved and green on the trunk
Does not merge, push, retarget, comment or approve anything

evals.name: what-should-i-merge-next
evals.expected_output: A short prioritised answer leading with PRs that are approved, CI-clean and based on the trunk, then the cheapest single unblock that frees the most downstream work. Not an exhaustive dump of every PR.
assertions: Leads with PRs that are approved, green and based on the trunk
Identifies the single cheapest action that unblocks the most other PRs
Respects bottom-up merge order within any stack it mentions
Stays brief rather than reproducing the full board

evals.name: refetch-delta
evals.expected_output: A refreshed board that leads with what changed since the previous report (newly approved, newly blocked, newly merged, no movement) before restating the full picture.
assertions: Leads with a delta section describing what changed since the prior report
Explicitly notes chains or PRs where nothing moved
Re-runs the fetch rather than reusing stale numbers from earlier in the conversation

evals.name: ci-failure-detail
evals.prompt: any of my PRs failing CI? what actually broke
evals.expected_output: For each PR with a red check, the specific failing test file, line and assertion pulled from the job log, plus a judgement on whether it is a real regression or a stale run from a superseded commit.
assertions: Drills into the failing job log rather than only naming the red check
Reports the failing test file, line and assertion text
Checks whether the failing run corresponds to the PR's current head commit
Distinguishes a real regression from flake or a stale run

should_not_trigger.prompt: what did the reviewer say on PR 7591? I need to work through their comments
should_not_trigger.reason: Single-PR feedback triage belongs to pr-review-feedback

should_not_trigger.prompt: can you review PR 7663 for me, Ben asked me to take a look
should_not_trigger.reason: Producing a fresh review of someone else's PR belongs to pr-dual-review

should_not_trigger.prompt: split this branch up into stacked PRs, the diff is about 2000 lines now
should_not_trigger.reason: Creating a stack belongs to stacked-delivery. pr-board only reports on stacks that already exist
